researched_by: the council's own motorhome and caravan parking page, car park charges page and coastal PSPO page, cross-read against the text of the Off-Street Parking Places Order (2003 and 2022 versions), the February 2026 charges order notice, the adopted Parking Strategy, and local news coverage of the 2025 policy change
policy_summary:
Thanet has just done the thing almost no English district does: it removed its own prohibition on sleeping. The Off-Street Parking Places Order has carried a bare 'no sleeping or camping' article since at least the 2003 consolidation - Article 29 then, Article 35 in the 2022 version - so for two decades a motorhome could legally BUY a 24-hour ticket in a Thanet car park and still commit a contravention by going to bed in it. In October 2025 the council announced it would scrap that rule, and the current guidance is now unambiguous: 'You may sleep within your vehicle overnight in the designated spaces.'

The designated spaces are five coastal car parks with five motorhome and caravan bays each - St Mildreds Bay at Westgate-on-Sea, Minnis Bay at Birchington, Barnes at Westbrook in Margate, Joss Bay at Broadstairs and Marina Esplanade at Ramsgate - about 25 bays across the whole isle. A 24-hour ticket costs GBP13.00, raised from GBP12.50 by the charges order made on 5 February 2026 and effective from 1 April 2026; it was GBP10 in the 2022 order. Charges apply 7am to 10pm every day, all year, which means the motorhome rate is one of the few things in Thanet you still pay for in winter when car parking on the bays is free. Payment is pay and display machine or RingGo, except at Barnes, which is RingGo only. There is no maximum stay and no return gap published. There are no waste or water facilities at any of the five - the council says so in terms.

Everything outside those bays is closed, and closed twice over. The parking order's own construction does the first half: Article 42 of the 2022 order provides that no minibus or motor caravan shall use a parking place unless otherwise stated, so a motorhome in an ordinary bay in an ordinary Thanet car park is not merely sleeping in the wrong place, it is parked in a place it is not permitted to use at all. The second half is the Thanet Beaches and Coast PSPO 2024, in force 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2027, which prohibits 'camping or the erection and occupation of any structure (this includes but is not exclusive to vehicles, tents, marquees, yurts and any other temporary building) being used to occupy land ... on beaches, promenades, clifftops, nearby green spaces, car parks and surrounding areas of the public realm without prior consent of the Council'. That clause names vehicles and names car parks. The designated motorhome bays work as the council's consent; everywhere else on the Thanet coast, occupying a vehicle overnight is a PSPO breach carrying a fixed penalty, not just a parking contravention.

What pushed all this was displacement. Kent County Council, not Thanet, holds the on-street powers, and KCC has banned motor caravans overnight on Ramsgate's Western Undercliff and Royal Harbour Approach since September 2020 and on Cliff Road, The Parade, Sea Road, Royal Esplanade and Palm Bay Avenue across Birchington, Westgate and Margate since the 2021 order. Vans went onto residential streets instead, which is lawful, and residents complained. Cllr George Kup's motion to full council in October 2025 - GBP10-12 a night, 48 hours maximum with no return within 72, self-contained only, no awnings or barbecues, online booking - was the response. The council did not adopt the motion's terms wholesale, but it did adopt its direction, and Action 15 of the 2024 Parking Strategy had already committed it to considering overnight motorhome parking in suitable car parks.
notes:
The interesting thing here is that Thanet went the opposite way to the rest of this dataset. North Devon, Dover and most English districts write 'no sleeping' into the ancillary conditions of the off-street order and leave it there. Thanet HAD that condition, found it absurd - you could pay for 24 hours and not use them - and took it out for the designated bays. That is the first clear example in the dataset of an English district repealing a sleeping prohibition rather than adding one, and it happened because the council decided motorhome tourism was worth having rather than because anyone forced it.

Read the two instruments together and the regime is coherent in a way most are not. The parking order says WHERE a motor caravan may park (five car parks, nowhere else). The PSPO says WHERE it may be occupied (only with council consent, which the bays are). So a van in an undesignated Thanet car park overnight is exposed on both counts, and the PSPO limb has a fixed penalty attached, which is a sharper instrument than a PCN.

A TRAP IN THE DRAFTING. The 2022 order defines 'Motor Caravan' as 'a motor vehicle not exceeding 5.5m in length which provides fixed sleeping arrangements'. That is a hard length cap buried in a definition, not in a condition, and 5.5m is small - it admits a Transit-based conversion and a compact coachbuilt and excludes most 6m-plus motorhomes, which then fall outside the definition of the very vehicle the bays are for. Nothing on the council's public page mentions a length limit. Whether the 2025 consolidation kept the 5.5m figure is the single most consequential unresolved point in this file.

Bay counts do not agree with themselves. The motorhome page says five bays at each of the five car parks; the car park charges page says three at Joss Bay and does not list Marina Esplanade at all; Thanet Guide's per-car-park data says four at St Mildreds Bay, four at Marina Esplanade and five at Minnis Bay and Barnes, and none at Joss Bay. Twenty-five is the council's own headline figure and is used here, but the real number is probably nearer twenty, and Joss Bay is the one to check.

Direction of travel: expanding, publicly and deliberately. Seventeen bays in October 2025, twenty-five now, with the council's stated target 'up to 30 spaces' and black waste disposal 'being considered'. Cllr Bright's line was 'sooner rather than later'. Marina Esplanade at Ramsgate was already in the 2022 order as an all-year motor caravan location, so the growth since 2025 is really St Mildreds Bay plus increased bay counts rather than wholly new sites - and the promised further Broadstairs and Ramsgate locations have not appeared.

ENFORCEMENT REALITY. Thanet's own FOI answer on overnight restrictions is candid: the driver was 'people were living in their caravans/campervans overnight on the highway which leads to the health and safety risk of there being a collision with a vehicle occupied by persons asleep', plus 'noise, waste and rubbish issues', and the evidence base was Broadstairs & St Peter's Town Council's complaint file - the district ran no survey of its own and considered none necessary. The same answer concedes a heading error in the order, restrictions sitting under 'Prohibition of Stopping Outside Schools' when they belonged under 'Prohibition of Waiting', which the council maintains is still enforceable. That is the quality of evidence and drafting behind the Thanet restrictions.

And the hard cases are not being handled by parking law at all. When 19 caravans, campers and motorhomes had settled at Ramsgate's Western Undercliff by June 2026, some for over a year, it was KENT COUNTY COUNCIL that served 24-hour notices to leave after welfare checks - land powers on KCC land, not a Thanet PCN and not the PSPO. Long-term vehicle dwelling in Thanet is a housing and welfare problem wearing a parking problem's clothes, and the aire is not an answer to it.

NOT THANET'S: every on-street restriction in the district, including all five seafront roads and both Ramsgate clifftop roads, belongs to Kent County Council and is recorded in the Kent County Council file.

PROVISION THE PARKING PAGES DO NOT MENTION - CHECKED, NONE FOUND (27 July 2026). Thanet's parks and open spaces, harbour and locations pages were searched separately from the parking pages. The district has no country park; the council describes its estate as 'over 70 parks and open spaces, including areas such as recreation grounds, churchyards and memorial gardens', over 30 play areas, two skate parks, sports grounds and cemeteries - all day use, none with camping. The council owns and runs Ramsgate Royal Harbour, but its harbour permits are boat permits: the only overnight provision there is the 'Ramsgate Marina Live on Board' permit for people 'with permission to live on board their vessels', which is a vessel arrangement and not a vehicle one, and the Royal Harbour multi-storey closes all floors above the ground floor between 19:00 and 07:00. Western Undercliff, where 19 caravans, campers and motorhomes were served notice to leave in June 2026, is a beach frontage with roadside bays next to the Port of Ramsgate, not a site the council provides. No council-owned caravan park, touring site or holiday park was found, and Thanet has not been reorganised, so there is no inherited district caravan site. The district's touring supply is entirely private - Nethercourt Touring Park at Ramsgate is the nearest example - and none of it should be recorded under this authority. The only movement towards council provision is the October 2025 members' motion for a paid overnight motorhome pilot at GBP10-GBP12 a night, 48 hours maximum, self-contained vehicles only, at two coastal locations; that is a parking scheme rather than a campsite and its status is already covered above.
open_questions: Does the Thanet District Council (Off-Street Parking Places) (Consolidation) Order 2025 keep the 5.5m length cap in the definition of 'Motor Caravan'? The order is published only as a Google Doc link from the council's TRO page and could not be retrieved. If the cap survives, most motorhomes on the road today are outside the scheme.

Exactly which article of the current order was amended or revoked to permit sleeping, and whether the permission is written into the order or is only guidance. The council's web page says 'You may sleep within your vehicle overnight in the designated spaces'; the corresponding order text was not obtained.
The real bay count at Joss Bay. The motorhome page says 5, the car park charges page says 3, and Thanet Guide's Joss Bay entry lists no motor caravan bays at all in a 36-space car park.

Is there a maximum stay? Nothing published caps consecutive nights or imposes a return gap, which would make Thanet unusually permissive - Cllr Kup's motion proposed 48 hours with a 72-hour return gap and it is not clear whether that was adopted.
Are the bays bookable, and is there a self-containment requirement? The motion proposed both; the council's page mentions neither, and says only that no waste or water facilities are provided.
Whether the GBP13 24-hour ticket can be bought outside the 7am-10pm charging window, and what a van arriving at 10.30pm is supposed to do.
The fixed penalty amount under the Thanet Beaches and Coast PSPO 2024, and whether the camping clause has ever actually been used against an occupied vehicle in a car park.
Whether the further Broadstairs and Ramsgate motorhome locations promised in October 2025, and the black waste disposal point, have progressed. Nothing was published by July 2026.
Whether the Marina Esplanade car park's possible disposal - it appeared on a January 2026 list of properties the council was considering selling - puts those bays at risk.

sites.name: Minnis Bay Car Park, Birchington
sites.search_hint: Minnis Bay car park, The Parade, Birchington
sites.notes: The westernmost of the five and the one named in the register as a pressure point. Five motor caravan and caravan bays in a 154-space car park on The Parade, directly behind the beach. GBP13 for 24 hours, charged 7am-10pm all year - note that ordinary car parking here is FREE from 1 November to 31 March but the motorhome tariff is not, so in winter you are the only vehicle paying. Sleeping in the vehicle is permitted in the designated bays. No waste or water facilities. Was in the 2022 order at GBP10 as a seasonal 1 April-31 October motor caravan location; it is now charged year-round. THE PARADE, the road this car park stands on, is one of the streets where Kent County Council prohibits motor caravans parking 6pm-6am - the bay is legal, the kerb outside it is not.

sites.notes: The newest of the five - it does not appear in the 2022 order's motor caravan schedule and was added as part of the post-2025 expansion. Sixty-three spaces on Old Boundary Road, the old Westgate/Westbrook boundary, a short walk above the bay. The council's motorhome page says five motorhome bays; Thanet Guide says four. GBP13 for 24 hours, charged 7am-10pm; ordinary cars park free in winter, motorhomes do not. Sleeping permitted in the designated bays; no waste or water. SEA ROAD, the seafront road serving this bay, carries Kent County Council's 6pm-6am motor caravan prohibition.

sites.name: Barnes Car Park, Westbrook, Margate
sites.search_hint: Barnes car park, Royal Esplanade, Westbrook, Margate
sites.notes: THE SHARPEST ILLUSTRATION OF THE TWO-AUTHORITY REGIME IN KENT. Five motorhome bays in a 137-space car park on Royal Esplanade - and Royal Esplanade is one of the five roads on which Kent County Council prohibits motor caravans parking between 6pm and 6am. Park in the bay and you may sleep; park at the kerb outside and you get a PCN. Neither council's website explains the other's rule. RINGGO ONLY - there is no pay and display machine here, which matters if you arrive without signal or a UK phone. GBP13 for 24 hours, charged 7am-10pm, all year; free for cars in winter but not for motorhomes. Was in the 2022 order as a seasonal 1 April-31 October motor caravan location at GBP10.

The motorhome page says five bays, the council's own car park charges page says three, and Thanet Guide's entry lists none. Five is used here because it is the council's headline figure, but this is the site to verify before relying on it. GBP13 for 24 hours, charged 7am-10pm; sleeping permitted in the designated bays; no waste or water. Was in the 2022 order as a seasonal 1 April-31 October motor caravan location at GBP10.

sites.name: Marina Esplanade Car Park, Ramsgate
sites.notes: The only one of the five that is not a beach car park and the only one that was an ALL-YEAR motor caravan location in the 2022 order rather than a seasonal one - so Ramsgate provision is older than the 2025 announcement implies. A large 244-space car park below the East Cliff, open 24 hours, walkable to the Royal Harbour. Five motorhome bays per the council's page, four per Thanet Guide. GBP13 for 24 hours, sleeping permitted in the designated bays, no waste or water. TWO CAUTIONS: the car park appeared on a January 2026 list of council properties being considered for sale, and the site has a history of unauthorised encampments. It is also the nearest legal option to Western Undercliff and Royal Harbour Approach, where Kent County Council bans overnight parking by anything other than a car or motorcycle and cleared 19 vehicles in June 2026.

sites.name: All other Thanet District Council car parks
sites.notes: Article 42 of the Off-Street Parking Places Order provides that 'No Minibus or Motor Caravan shall use a Parking Place unless otherwise stated'. The permission is therefore an allowlist, not a general right: a motor caravan may use the five designated car parks and no others, whatever the time of day and whether or not anyone is sleeping in it. Article 35 of the same order separately prohibits use of a parking place 'for sleeping or camping purposes' - the article the council announced in October 2025 it would scrap; the current guidance permits sleeping in the designated bays, but the wording of the 2025 consolidation could not be read, so whether Article 35 survives for the rest of the estate is unconfirmed. Note also the definition: 'Motor Caravan' means 'a motor vehicle not exceeding 5.5m in length which provides fixed sleeping arrangements', a length cap that appears nowhere in the council's public guidance. Enforced by penalty charge notice.

sites.name: Thanet Beaches and Coast PSPO 2024
sites.notes: In force 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2027, extendable by three years. The operative clause names vehicles and names car parks: 'Camping or the erection and occupation of any structure (this includes but is not exclusive to vehicles, tents, marquees, yurts and any other temporary building) being used to occupy land is not permitted on beaches, promenades, clifftops, nearby green spaces, car parks and surrounding areas of the public realm without prior consent of the Council with the exception of sun shades.' So occupying a vehicle overnight anywhere on the Thanet coast is a PSPO breach unless the council has consented - which is what the five designated bays are. A separate clause bans driving or parking any motorised vehicle on promenades and beaches, mobility scooters and e-bikes excepted. Enforced by fixed penalty notice issued by an authorised person, a different and sharper route than a parking PCN. Geographic extent is defined by a mapped schedule that was not retrievable, so this is recorded as a zone rather than a place.

sites.name: Broadstairs Harbour Car Park
sites.search_hint: Broadstairs Harbour car park, Harbour Street, Broadstairs
sites.notes: The one place in the Thanet estate where the order historically went beyond 'no sleeping' and prohibited the overnight PARKING itself: the 2003 order's schedule gave Broadstairs Harbour a 12-hour maximum with 'no overnight parking' between 1 May and 30 September. The current harbour charges page shows the car park operating 7am-10pm only, 69 spaces, with seasonal tariffs, which is consistent with the prohibition surviving in substance, but the express condition was not found in a current order and this is recorded at low confidence. Ramsgate's harbour car parks by contrast run 24/7 and Westcross Wall sells 24-hour, 5-day and 28-day tickets - but none of them is a designated motor caravan location, so Article 42 shuts a motorhome out regardless.
